ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A partial food web is shown below. The bird species in this food web are owls and hawks. If an animal that preys on birds enters the community, what will most likely happen to the plant populations?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The food web diagram shows the bird species as a hawk and an owl. Arrows point from prey animals such as mouse, snake, and frog toward the hawk or owl, indicating that these birds eat those animals. The diagram also shows plant producers such as grass and trees, with arrows from grass or trees toward primary consumers such as mouse, cricket, and deer. Reasoning: If a new animal that preys on birds enters the community, the hawk and owl populations would likely decline. With fewer hawks and owls, some of the animals they normally eat, especially plant-eating or plant-linked animals like mice, would likely increase. More plant consumers would put more feeding pressure on grass and other plants. Therefore, the plant populations would most likely decrease.
